# OpenTakeoff

> The takeoff software for agents: a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) construction takeoff engine that an AI agent and a person drive the same way. Open a plan (PDF, image, or .zip plan set), set the scale, trace rooms and runs under finish conditions, apply waste % and supporting materials, and export quantities (SF/SY/LF/EA) plus a marked-up planset PDF. A person uses the browser canvas; an agent calls the same geometry and quantity modules over MCP (`npx -y opentakeoff-mcp`, {{TOOL_COUNT}} tools), with the scale, method and author of every measurement recorded. Built for flooring; the measuring tools work for any trade (drywall, paint, wall tile, concrete, sitework). No account. The canvas keeps plans in the browser.

OpenTakeoff is an open-source alternative to subscription takeoff software, built so an AI agent can drive the engine directly — not through screen scraping or a bolted-on chat layer. It is a static web app: self-hosting is one `npm run build` and any static file host. It measures; it does not price (no cost database in the box).

## Pages

- [Open the canvas](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/): the takeoff app in the browser, with a bundled sample plan (a real VA medical-center floor finish plan)
- [For agents](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/agents/): install the MCP server, the five-step standard finish, provenance and review, what data leaves the machine
- [Flooring takeoff](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/flooring-takeoff/): the working order on a real bid set, the report, roll goods (carpet, sheet vinyl) figured as cuts with seams
- [Free takeoff software](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/free-takeoff-software/): what is free, what it measures, honest limits
- [Calculators](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/tools/): [SF to SY](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/tools/sf-to-sy/), [waste, attic stock and cartons](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/tools/flooring-order-calculator/), [carpet roll cuts](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/tools/carpet-roll-calculator/), [wall base](https://opentakeoff.kentucky-ai.com/tools/base-calculator/)

## Key facts

- **Agents first**: the MCP server and the canvas share the geometry, calibration and quantity modules; an agent's export opens in the canvas as ordinary takeoff records. Every shape records its scale, method, and whether a person or an agent drew it.
- **MCP server**: `opentakeoff-mcp` on npm and the official MCP registry, {{TOOL_COUNT}} tools on a default build — load a plan, read the sheet, adopt the scale (never applied silently), measure rooms on the wall faces, derive base and transitions, check the work on a rendered overlay, and export a marked planset PDF. Claude Code: `claude mcp add opentakeoff -- npx -y opentakeoff-mcp`.
- **Review**: agent work lands as a dashed pending proposal; only a person at the canvas can approve it. Scales an agent sets are flagged unconfirmed until a person confirms them.
- **One-Click Area is temporarily gated** while the flood engine is re-validated; rooms are traced with Area (`A`) in the canvas and `measure_polygon` over MCP. `OPENTAKEOFF_ONE_CLICK=1` / `VITE_ONE_CLICK=1` lift the gate.
- Measuring: Area, Rectangle, Linear, Surface Area (walls, run × height), Count, Cut Out (deducts); stitched sheets across match lines
- Drawing aids: 45°/90° angle lock, live angle and segment-length readout, snap
- Scale: reads the drawn scale note per sheet for the user to adopt, or calibrate from a known dimension
- Conditions: color + CAD hatch per finish, waste %, multiplier, wall height, border thickness; import conditions from the finish schedule
- Roll goods: broadloom carpet, sheet vinyl and sheet rubber figured into numbered cuts with Roll Order LF, Rolls and Seam LF
- Reports: per-condition SF/SY/LF/EA measured and waste-adjusted, a supporting-materials buy list rounded to whole units; CSV, Excel, JSON and marked-set PDF export
- Data: the canvas stores projects in IndexedDB/localStorage; opening a plan uploads nothing. Over MCP the server runs locally, and the assistant receives the tool results it asks for (which can include drawing text, rendered images and quantities)
- Stack: React 18 + Vite + pdf.js; the whole app is a static build
- License: Apache-2.0 — [fork it](https://github.com/Kentucky-ai/opentakeoff/fork), ship it, build a product on it
- Maintained by Kentucky AI (applied AI R&D, Louisville, KY): https://kentucky-ai.com
